summary: Module 4 VERIFY. Bug #6: 2000-request check via tracemalloc inside the app process -- traced memory 1.57MB after warmup vs 11.17MB after +2000 GET /links (delta +9.6MB, far under the 50MB bar). Top allocations are import/anyio/asyncio internals; no DB Connection/Pool objects appear in any snapshot, and probe_conn_leak.py keeps Redis CLIENT LIST at baseline across forced error-path rounds. Why the finally fixes the leak: the connection must be released on every exit path -- success AND exception. If release stays in only the success branch, any error skips it and the pool leaks one connection per error request; after ~2000 error requests the pool is exhausted and the service dies. The fork's get_db() and analytics helpers already close in finally; the one remaining acquire-without-guaranteed-release path (cache.py aioredis clients) is now also closed in finally on all three functions. Bug #7: SQLAlchemy before_cursor_execute listener proves GET /links?limit=50 fires exactly 3 statements (user lookup, count, page SELECT) -- not 51; response time ~26-30ms (far under 200ms) for 50 rows. The N+1 pattern is absent in this fork, so there is no ORM-config regression to fix; the query log IS the evidence. Code-reading could not have caught a silent dependency-default change (the config would still read 'eager'); only observing the actual SQL emitted by the ORM at runtime reveals the N+1 -- that is why the tool-led probe is the right method.
